mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the last 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 3-month pre-rising period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by 2% or more in the same month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 20-day rolling IC remains below 0.05 and forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeds 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative and remain so across 10 consecutive such signals (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month coincides with a sharp drop in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence - so omit or use alternative), suggesting supply-side weakness that depresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior non-contraction months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (signaling tightening), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative due to the discounting of future cash flows at higher rates.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 12-month tightening phase (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not available) - instead, use HOUST (housing starts) as proxy: rapid increases in new housing starts (HOUST) during a declining unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4%) suggest economic resilience that supports equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and HOUST increases by 10% or more in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the signal (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime shift to inflationary expectations (not directly observable - so use CPIAUCSL trend), a sustained monthly CPIAUCSL increase above 0.4% for two months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as market anticipates rate stability.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeds 0.4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) and the CPIAUCSL trend reverses.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 50th percentile for three consecutive months while unemployment (UNRATE) is above 5%, it indicates a supply-side drag that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 50th percentile for 3 months and UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) or the supply shock reverses.
